==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|quykly}}, {{m|enm|quikliche}}, {{m|enm|quicliche}}, {{m|enm|cwikliche}}, {{m|enm|cwickliche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cwiculīċe}}. {{surf|en|quick|-ly|id2=adverbial}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkwɪk.li/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-quickly.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪkli|s=2}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|er,more}}

# {{1|rapidly}}; with [[speed]]; [[fast]]; with expedition.
#: {{syn|en|at speed|apace|lickety-split|q3=informal}}
#: {{ux|en|Luckily, the error was '''quickly''' corrected.}}
# Very [[soon]].
#: {{ux|en|If we go this way, we'll get there '''quickly'''.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Patrick Noack|title=Humans are terrible at planning for the future: Here's how we can change that|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/02/02/opinions/patrick-noack-future-long-term-thinking-spc-intl|date=2023-02-02|passage=There are eight principles in all, but three are really important if we want to shift '''quickly''' and inclusively toward a longer-term mode of thinking and acting.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230303181247/https://www.cnn.com/2023/02/02/opinions/patrick-noack-future-long-term-thinking-spc-intl/}}

====Usage notes====
* Although the comparative ([[quicklier]]) and superlative ([[quickliest]]) one-word forms exist and are and have been in limited use, the two-word forms (''more quickly'' and ''most quickly'') are much more common.

====Derived terms====
{{col2|en|as quickly as possible|death-come-quickly}}

====Related terms====
* {{l|en|quick}} {{qualifier|adjective and adverb}}
